issue_context.title: Videos with mkv ProjectionPoseRoll element are rotated in the wrong direction
issue_context.body:
### Important Information

Provide following Information:
- mpv version: 0.37.0 or 2024-03-31 daily build
- Platform and Version: Windows 10 or 11
- Source of the mpv binary: builds on the mpv website
- If known which version of mpv introduced the problem: I think support for ProjectionPoseRoll was introduced in 0.37.0
- GPU model, driver and version: various inted iGPUs
- Possible screenshot or video of visual glitches: N/A

### Reproduction steps

1. Use ffmpeg to rotate any video file and store it in an mkv container (ffmpeg -display_rotation 90 -i inputfilename -c copy output.mkv).
2. The ProjectionPoseRoll element will be set to 90.
3. Play the output file using ffplay. It will be rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise, which is correct.
4. Play the output file using mpv. It will be rotated 90 degrees clockwise, which is incorrect.

### Expected behavior

Positive ProjectionPoseRoll values should rotate counter-clockwise and negative values should rotate clockwise. Matroska element documentation for this is somewhat confusing, but it is clarified well in the technical notes linked below.

https://www.matroska.org/technical/notes.html#rotation

### Actual behavior

The video is rotated in the wrong direction by mpv during playback.

### Log file

[output.txt](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/files/14897715/output.txt)

### Sample files

Any video file rotated using ffmpeg (ffmpeg -display_rotation 90 -i inputfilename -c copy output.mkv).
comments:
Are you sure positive values should be counterclockwise? The actual specification is ambiguous since it doesn't specify what the "forward vector" is. https://www.matroska.org/technical/elements.html#ProjectionPoseRoll

Moreover, it seems like lavf is the odd one out here. mkvtoolnix/mpv/LAVFilters agree on positive values meaning clockwise rotation. You should probably open an issue on the specification repo first to get clarification

The actual specification is ambiguous, but the notes on matroska.org state direction that positive should be counter-clockwise. https://www.matroska.org/technical/notes.html#rotation

I'll open an issue on the specification repo as you suggest.

Another case of ambiguous Matroska spec?

Since we don't know which coordinate system author was referring when saying "forward vector", certain assumption has been made.

MPC-BE[1], MPC-HC, LAV Filters[2], ExoPlayer [3] and mpv [4] all agree on the current behavior. While as you rightfully pointed out libavformat [5] is not agreeing with the rest of the world. 

Also hubblec4 [6] and other similar texts follow what is done by the players, probably because he mentions MPC-BE and follow behavior of it.

I personally kinda agree that notes [7] makes strong argument against the current behavior. And I'll be honest mpv implementation is guilty of following all other players, simply because it works the same... 

[1] https://github.com/Aleksoid1978/MPC-BE/commit/4521f079fe63d655dd5b5add9991a8e2eccb67f8
[2] https://gitea.1f0.de/LAV/FFmpeg/commit/cf4386d4426223de6e70e144e16038998bbecefd
[3] https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/commit/fc6a1ea52264a5f2972602b3bbc90ad1fabba16c
[4] https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/commit/a4bf0bd695da7ac0fea561342c60d954d485af0a
[5] https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/commit/937bb6bbc1e8654633737e69e403e95a37113058
[6] https://github.com/hubblec4/Matroska-Playback/blob/611828239502e96e9e160c939ef39a089ea5ec97/src/Rotate.md
[7] https://www.matroska.org/technical/notes.html#rotation

Yes, "forward vector" was very unclear to me as well, and there are also forum threads I've read online where people are confused.

I assume now that it refers to the forward vector from the perspective of the viewer, so CCW rotation of the projection around it would result in a CCW rotation of the video. Hopefully the specification can be clarified.

> I assume now that it refers to the forward vector from the perspective of the viewer

If it is the case that the forward vector points from the viewer to the screen (and I think it's the only correct interpretation, given that these properties were designed for VR videos), a counter-clockwise rotation around that vector results in a clockwise rotation in the perspective of the viewer, based on right-hand rule.

So I think lavf is wrong here.

Ah, you're right, I accidentally reversed the direction in my head. So either "forward vector" must mean a vector normal to the plane of the screen pointing towards the viewer, or the notes on the Matroska website are incorrect, because they themselves state CCW.
Steve Lhomme has confirmed that the rotation should be counter-clockwise (https://github.com/ietf-wg-cellar/matroska-specification/issues/822).
I pinged interested parties in the above ticket, just to synchronize the change.

review_comments: Looking at this now, the inner-most `fmodf` could be removed, because Matroska spec require values to be [-180, 180], but it is fine as is. Just a remark I had in my head.
